analysis: The reference image shows a wheeled trash bin whose expected rigid parts are the main body, a hinged lid at the top, and two independently rotating wheels at the bottom (so 4 distinct rigid bodies are expected). The generated model decomposes into 3 parts total, and the grouping is mostly wrong. The lid is NOT separated from the main body — they are fused into a single rigid link, missing a major mechanical boundary. The two wheels ARE split off from the body into their own rigid unit (visible in the internal views — note that the external/internal split is just a rendering-visibility heuristic, so the wheels showing up on the internal side is a display artifact, not a geometric error). However, both wheels share the same color there, which means the model treats them as ONE rigid link rather than two independent wheels; a real trash bin must let each wheel rotate on its own axle. So out of the three main expected boundaries (lid-vs-body, wheel-vs-body, wheel-vs-wheel) only one is correctly drawn (wheel-vs-body). This is a weak decomposition but not a complete failure — score 2.
